design_rationale:
WHY THIS IS A GOOD TEST. A dual-eligible oxygen patient asks only to have his payment plan re-figured. The revision rule's prerequisite sentence makes the installment wait until the coinsurance charge of the newest oxygen line, dated after the Medicaid effective date, carries its crossover; the ledger shows September's does not. The agent must price that crossover the way Medicaid does — the oxygen month's fee composition under the QF rule, the flow multiplier, the usage and class shares, the lesser-of method and the sliding copay — and only then re-figure the arrangement from its record (months left, recent payments, new charges, rentals, tenure, secondary relief). Two six-factor computations, one value edge, one customer-owned write.

SCOPE. Draw (scripts/draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems 1, factor_counts [6, 6]. Occupied by task 0: hardship discount, prompt-pay discount, arrangement deposit, new-arrangement installment and their tools. Claimed here: coverage_ext_medicaid_crossover (post_crossover_payment_b661a2ed) and coverage_ext_arrangement_revision (revise_payment_arrangement_5f5b46f9). Disjoint from task 0: a different subject (coverage_secondary_payment) and a different write (revising an active arrangement, not opening one); after this task every extended policy of the difficulty is claimed exactly once.

PROBLEM-TREE CARD. Root: coverage_ext_arrangement_revision (owner=user). Edge: revision <- crossover, value_input on m_balance, state form, negated direction: 'A revised installment is not fixed until the coinsurance charge stemming from the newest oxygen line the primary adjudicated, when that line's date of service is on or after the Medicaid record's effective date, carries the crossover payment that Medicaid owes on it.' Opening evidence: the 2026-09-09 coinsurance charge (51.78) is after the Medicaid effective date 2026-04-01 and no secondary payment points at it (the latest crossover, 2026-08-20, points at the August charge). Exactly one write of the difficulty books a crossover payment (post_crossover_payment_b661a2ed). Four-point test: 'not ... until' joins the revision's own result to a record-visible state (a crossover row on each such charge), no tool/id/code token, hard wait scoped to the coinsurance charge of the newest oxygen line, dated on or after the effective date. Derivation: sentence + ledger (September charge without a crossover) + crossover rule -> post the crossover. Order: crossover, revision. Deletion sensitivity: skip crossover -> 30.57 instead of 29.11. Persona never names the crossover; tools validate nothing.

BASE-INVARIANT CARD. coverage_secondary_payment (step 10): coverage_agg_coordination.secondary_record_standing — the Medicaid record is active (bound to payer_coverage_id); Medicaid is the payer of last resort and Medicare's secondary_crossover_automatic is true, so no separate claim or filing window is involved; a secondary payment never exceeds the charge's open amount (14.66 <= 51.78, the charge unpaid). coverage_agg_payment_allocation: a secondary payment settles only the charge it adjudicated. coverage_payment_plan_set (step 12): plan_agreement_signed — the 2026-04-14 payment_plan_agreement on the Medicare account is approved; plan_account_standing — the Medicare record is active. No time-kind gate governs these subjects (temporal_feasibility empty).

BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD. Crossover target: the coinsurance charge of oxygen month 16 (2026-09-09), linked to its oxygen_billing line (adjudicated 2026-09-21, allowed 258.92, Medicare paid 207.14). Excluded: months 11-15 (each already has its crossover: 18.81 for months 11-12, 11.57 for months 13-15), months 1-10 (before Medicaid). Revision target: the arrangement on the Medicare account (active since 2026-05-01, 49.02). Installments named no charge and were split oldest-first over the 2025 coinsurance charges and the January deductible charge; the month remainders after each crossover were paid against their own months.

FACTOR CARD.
Crossover (14.66; all-baseline 0.00, because the standard rate (172.61 + 28.43) x 82% = 164.85 is below Medicare's payment of 207.14):
- flow multiplier 1.5: without it -> 0.00.
- add-on reckoning (method): the higher-of rule leaves no add-on; the full add-on -> 39.23.
- usage share 90: the whole rate -> 39.52.
- class rate share 100: 82% -> 0.00.
- rental-phase share 96 (month 16): the whole rate -> 23.98.
- copay band 1.90 (cost share 51.78): the class copay 3.00 -> 13.56.
Every factor reads only its own oxygen records.
Revision (29.11; all-baseline 25.00, the floor of 291.08 / 12):
- core term kept at 6: counted afresh -> 25.00.
- rental burden 1: -> 32.34.
- new charges 1: -> 32.34.
- installment record 2: -> 36.39.
- long coverage 2: -> 36.39.
- secondary relief 2 off: -> 25.00.
The new-charge factor now reads its own arrangement-start window. Cross-difficulty factors read oxygen. Multi-source: the core-term convention.

SEED ROWS. Medicare record (balance 305.74; accumulators consistent), Medicaid record (no balance), the approved 2026-04-14 agreement (requested 588.29 = balance that day), the oxygen record (rental since 2025-06-09, flow raised to 4.5 LPM by the 2026-08-25 order) and its sixteen paid months (QF from September), and the ledger: 17 charges (16 months; January wholly deductible, February split into deductible and coinsurance), 2 deductible and 15 oop accumulator rows plus the 2026-01-01 oop reset, payments (two 2025 checks, five month remainders, six installments split oldest-first), five crossovers (18.81 for months 11-12, 11.57 for months 13-15), statements (cycles counted from the last zero balance) and eligibility responses on both records. No base automatic clause fires: no credit, no small balance, the arrangement blocks collections, eligibility is fresh.

PERSONA. Volunteered: the higher September bill and the request to redo the plan. Given only on request: name/phone, birthday, ZIP/email, insurance, the flow change, the usage pattern. Passive: acknowledges a Medical Assistance payment if told, accepts the re-figured installment and makes the change himself, closes. No further asks.

STANDARD SOLUTION AND VERIFICATION. Reads: profile, identity, coverage records, ledger, requests, oxygen record and billing, wheelchair and PAP checks. Writes: crossover 14.66 on the September charge (payer Medicaid); patient revises installment to 29.11. Verification code (gold replayed with the real erlbench tools, each compute evaluated with check_compute.build_env / eval_compute just before its step, factor baselines substituted one by one and together) output: crossover 14.66 (round-4 figures: baseline 0.00; factors 0 / 39.23 / 39.52 / 0 / 23.98 / 13.56), revision 29.11 (baseline 25.0; factors 25.0 / 32.34 / 32.34 / 36.39 / 36.39 / 25.0), skip-crossover revision 30.57.

TRAPS. (1) Revising on the opening balance 305.74. (2) Treating the 588.29 on the April agreement as the balance. (3) Counting the arrangement afresh at 12 months. (4) Paying 100 percent of the cost share as base coordination says for Medicaid, instead of the lesser-of crossover price. (5) Pricing the month at the add-on composition or at 3.0 LPM.

DRAFT RECOMPUTATION FROM THE VISIBLE CONTEXT. The revision rule sends the reader to the September charge; the crossover rule with the oxygen record and line gives 14.66; the revision rule then gives 29.11 — the same as gold.

GATES (run from the repository root, per task with --task N and then difficulty-wide): check_extended EXTENDED OK; check_task_tools TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK (6 tools); replay_tasks REPLAY OK (0.json closure 70/70, 1.json 108/108, deterministic, non-vacuous, no Error); check_solvability SOLVABILITY OK; check_compute COMPUTE OK (round 3: suite branches mean 71.00, steps mean 15.50, history_rows_max 80, branches_max 90); check_grounding GROUNDING OK; check_cache_diff informational only (no cache trap designed); check_cross_fire SCOPE OK. check_traceability is run after the KB is rendered.

ROUND 2 REWORK (policy-task audit 1.md / _difficulty.md). T1-1/F-1: the copay ladder no longer carries the date-of-service conjunct that restated the policy's scope; it now divides recipients by qmb_status and by the Medicare cost share Medicaid is asked to pay (bands 10 / 45 / 75), read from the line itself. The September line's 51.78 falls in the (45, 75] band (1.90) while the April-August lines' 40.21 sat in (10, 45] (1.30), so the seeded crossovers stay consistent and the scored crossover moves from 15.26 to 14.66; the revision moves from 29.05 to 29.11 (291.08 / 10). O-5: the overwrite of the base coinsurance clause now names the whole replacement quantity (price less copayment); the rule now scopes the crossover to coinsurance charges, leaves deductible charges to the base deductible clause, prices from the newest oxygen line and settles the coinsurance charge stemming from that line (E-5), and caps the payment at the charge's open amount, which compute implements as MN with the line's cost share for a charge carrying no payment or adjustment. E-6: every RND now rounds half up (a 0.000001 nudge before Python round). F-2: the revision core term's second tier re-anchors on the benefit year instead of adding a constant. O-6: the revise tool no longer writes payment_plan_status. Re-run: crossover 14.66 (round-4 figures: baseline 0.00; factors 0 / 39.23 / 39.52 / 0 / 23.98 / 13.56), revision 29.11 (baseline 25.00; factors 25.00 / 32.34 / 32.34 / 36.39 / 36.39 / 25.00), skip-crossover revision 30.57.

ROUND 3 REWORK (N-1 class, closed here though it did not bear on this world). The crossover grant sentence now says Medicaid crosses over each oxygen line while it is the newest line the primary has adjudicated, and that a coinsurance charge from an older line left without a crossover was refused at its turn and stays with the patient (wording superseded in round 4 by newest-first posting order); the figuring sentence and compute price that newest line alone, and the revision's prerequisite sentence waits on the coinsurance charge of the newest oxygen line. World check (task 1): the newest line is month 16 (2026-09-09); its charge is the only in-scope charge without a crossover, and the April-August charges carry theirs. Values unchanged: crossover 14.66, revision 29.11.

ROUND 4 REWORK (render-source mismatches 1-2, 11, 13-14; N3-2, N3-4). The crossover is rebuilt so that each factor reads only its own records. The Medicaid monthly rate is now part of the baseline (standard fee x Medicaid allowed percent, priced with the standard lesser-of method). The flow multiplier, the add-on reckoning (with its own flow and use reads), the usage, rate and new rental-phase shares, and the copay band each replace one default. The pricing-method factor, which consumed the combined rate, is gone. The cap is stated exactly as compute applies it (never more than the line's cost share) through a scoped overwrite of the base open-amount sentence. The base coinsurance-share clause stays in force for every other secondary payment. The 'refused at its turn' clause is replaced by newest-first posting order. World patch: under the rental-phase share, months 11-12 now take the whole rate, so their crossovers are 18.81 and the patient's remainders 21.40; months 13-15 keep 11.57. Statement balances and the account balance are unchanged. Gold is unchanged: crossover 14.66, revision 29.11, skip-crossover 30.57.
user_scenario:
You are Calvin Ostrowski, 77, a retired machinist from Coraopolis who has been on home oxygen from Summit Ridge Home Medical since June of last year. You speak slowly and politely and keep all your bills in a folder by the phone. You open by explaining that your lung doctor turned your oxygen up at the end of August, that the bill for September came in higher, and that with the monthly payment-plan amount you set up in April on top of it you can't keep up. You ask: "Could you redo my monthly payment plan so it covers what I owe now?" You want the plan itself changed today, on this call, and you are not asking for anything to be refunded or written off.

Only when the agent asks who you are do you say "my name is Calvin Ostrowski and my phone number is 4125550562"; to confirm your identity you say "my birthday is 1949-08-22", and if one more detail is wanted you give your ZIP code, 15108, or your email, cal.ostrowski49@yahoo.com. If the agent asks what insurance you have, you say Medicare, and since April also the Pennsylvania Medical Assistance card. If the agent asks about the oxygen change, you say the doctor raised you to four and a half liters at the end of August; if asked how you use it, you say when you're up and about and at night. You don't remember any account or claim numbers and you don't know what anything should come to.

You never suggest an amount, a step or an order of steps. If the agent tells you that a payment from Medical Assistance is being put on your account, you say that's good to hear and let them carry on. When the agent tells you the new monthly amount and hands you the step to change the plan, you accept that amount — you don't want to pay more each month than that — and you make the change yourself. Once the agent tells you the plan has been changed, you thank them and say goodbye; you have nothing else to ask.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 14.66. Line: the newest oxygen line the primary adjudicated is month 16 (date of service 2026-09-09, adjudicated 2026-09-21): cost share 51.78, Medicare paid 207.14. Medicaid monthly rate: stationary 172.61 x flow multiplier 1.5 (prescribed_lpm 4.5 > 4) = 258.915, plus the portable add-on as reckoned (flow above 4 with portable cylinders and use not sleep_only: only the part by which 172.61 + 28.43 = 201.04 exceeds 258.915, so 0), times usage share 90 (exertion_and_sleep), rate share 100 (portable cylinders) and rental-phase share 96 (month 16, from month 13) = 223.70. Crossover price: lesser of 51.78 and 223.70 - 207.14 = 16.56 -> 16.56. Copay: not_qmb, cost share 51.78 in (45, 75] -> 1.90. Payment 16.56 - 1.90 = 14.66, not above the cost share 51.78.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.coverage_id: 2c7eb87d-36f1-45e7-8585-373aaf663280. Basis: the crossover rule 'one secondary-payment entry on the primary account' and the docstring 'the primary coverage account that carries the charge'; the Original Medicare record is the primary (coverage_priority primary) and the charge sits on it. Uniqueness: the Medicaid record is secondary and carries no charges.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.applied_to_entry_id: 24fc45fc-3e67-4e2a-9daa-ff8a01a8f2d8. Basis: the crossover rule 'every coinsurance charge the primary leaves on an oxygen claim line whose date of service falls on or after the Medicaid record's effective_date receives the Medicaid crossover payment' and 'the crossover figured is worked from that line ... and it settles the coinsurance charge that stems from that line', the line being the newest oxygen line the primary adjudicated (month 16). Uniqueness: the April-August coinsurance charges already carry crossover rows (2026-04-23..2026-08-20); the charges before 2026-04-01 predate Medicaid; only the 2026-09-09 coinsurance charge (51.78) lacks one.

Basis: the rule '... carrying the Medicaid record as payer_coverage_id' and the docstring 'the secondary coverage record that paid'. Uniqueness: the Medicaid Fee-for-Service record is the patient's only secondary record.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona asks only for the plan to be re-figured. Neither coverage_ext_medicaid_crossover nor any rule wording occurs in user_scenario.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: post_crossover_payment_b661a2ed reads the coverage record and the charge only to copy customer_id, the balance, the allowed amount and the line's origin, then creates one secondary-payment row and updates the balance; revise_payment_arrangement_5f5b46f9 only updates the arrangement's installment. Neither checks whether a crossover is owed or posted, neither refuses, neither hints; revising before the crossover simply records an installment figured on the wrong balance.
